body.statement: On any ordered grid \(\mathcal G_m\), \(f^x\) belongs to \(\mathcal N_x\) if and only if it is feasible for the nested-survivor chain flow, equivalently if \(\sum_{i>k}f^x_{ij}\le\kappa^x_{kj}\) for every \(k,j\) together with its two margins. The network has \(O(m^2)\) nodes and arcs when both time axes have \(m\) levels, every feasible flow lifts to a full law, and \(h_m(c)\) equals the stated node-potential dual for every signed cost \(c\).
body.justification: The quadratic reduction makes exact joint-surface support computation possible and exposes the complete capacity constraints rather than hiding them in a four-time table.
body.gap: Russell and Ober-Reynolds provide generic latent-law programs and duals; neither source gives this nested chain, its complete suffix cuts, or the reconstruction of full semicompeting-risk laws.
body.consumer: It supplies an exact auditable algorithm for the finite-horizon grids used in the Comment et al. analysis and a certificate for every reported support endpoint.
